stories.headline: Vikings' Murray clears concussion protocol, will start vs. Bucs
stories.summary: Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray has cleared the concussion protocol and will start Sunday's game at the Buccaneers, coach Kevin O'Connell announced Monday.
stories.body:
Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray has cleared the concussion protocol and will start Sunday's game at the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, coach Kevin O'Connell announced Monday.

Murray suffered his concussion on the 11th play of his debut game with the Vikings in Week 1 against the Green Bay Packers, but his symptoms were minor enough to allow him to practice.

Backup Carson Wentz has completed 23 of 39 passes for 276 yards and three touchdowns since replacing Murray, without committing a turnover, and he made two throws in the fourth quarter Sunday that helped the Vikings drain clock while protecting a one-score lead in a 9-3 victory over the Chicago Bears.

The Vikings are 2-0, the lone undefeated team in the NFC North this season.

ESPN's Kevin Seifert contributed to this report.

stories.headline: Nicolas Batum announces retirement after 18 NBA seasons
stories.summary: Nicolas Batum has announced his retirement after 18 NBA seasons. A mainstay of the French national team, Batum played most of his NBA career with the Clippers, Hornets and Blazers.
stories.body:
Nicolas Batum, a longtime NBA forward and stalwart for France's national team, announced his retirement Monday in a social media video with his son.

"Yeah, that's it," Batum said. "Dad's done playing basketball. I've been playing for a long time. ... Twenty years as a pro. That's a lot. Eighteen years in the NBA. Fifteen with the French national team. ... It's over."

Batum, 37, spent most of the past six seasons with the LA Clippers, including averaging 4.0 points and 2.5 rebounds per game in 74 appearances last season. The 2008 first-round pick entered the NBA as a teenager and spent his first seven seasons with the Portland Trail Blazers before a lengthy stint with the Charlotte Hornets and a brief stop with the Philadelphia 76ers during the 2023-24 season.

Prior to joining the NBA, Batum played two seasons in the French league.

"I decided to retire from basketball for several reasons," Batum told his 10-year-old son, Ayden, in the video. "I want to come home and be with you. I'm going to take care of you and make room for others. I think I've done my time. My time with France ended two years ago. And the NBA is over too. You know, when you've played as much basketball as I have, at some point, you have to know when to stop. ... I've done everything I needed to do."

A versatile forward capable of defending multiple positions and stretching opposing defenses with his outside shot, Batum posted career averages of 9.6 points, 4.7 rebounds and 3.0 assists per game while shooting 37.1% on 3-pointers. During his career, Batum appeared in 76 playoff games and reached the 2021 Western Conference finals with the Clippers.

The native of Lisieux, France, was deeply committed to representing his country on the international stage, competing with longtime teammates Rudy Gobert and Evan Fournier. Batum started for French teams that won silver medals at the 2020 and 2024 Olympics, he won bronze medals at the 2014 and 2019 FIBA World Cups, and he medaled at the 2011, 2013 and 2015 EuroBasket tournaments.

Batum said in the video that France's semifinal win over Germany at the 2024 Olympics in Paris was "the best basketball moment I've ever experienced."

Earlier this summer, the Clippers declined their option on Batum's $5.9 million contract for the 2026-27 season, leaving him as an unrestricted free agent.

stories.headline: Formula 1 races to be 15 kilometres shorter from 2027 after FIA agrees reduction
stories.summary: Formula 1 races will be two to three laps shorter from 2027 after the FIA agreed a reduction.
stories.body:
Formula 1 races will be two to three laps shorter from 2027 after the FIA agreed a reduction.

The Formula 1 Commission met in London on Monday, chaired by chief executive Stefano Domenicali and single-seater director Nikolas Tombazis, and approved some regulatory tweaks.

These included a lower total race distance, going down from 305 kilometres to 290km to align with incoming power unit guidelines around fuel flow.

It was also decided that grands prix interrupted by rain or other factors would now be subject to a 'hard stop' time, but the obligation to complete a race within three hours from the start would be removed.

The changes will come into effect for a 2027 season which is again set to feature 24 grands prix, with Portugal and Türkiye returning to the calendar.

Formula 1 will also expand its sprint programme from six to 10 events, with Monaco among the most notable additions.

The famous street circuit has become known its lack of overtaking opportunities, often leaving qualifying as the highlight of a race weekend.

- Toto Wolff warned Michael Masi against being 'stubborn, arrogant' before F1 2021 title controversy

- Lando Norris backs 'exciting' 2027 Monaco GP sprint weekend but 'tougher for us drivers'

- Saunders: I raced against Max Verstappen ... for 10 seconds: Inside the chaos of Max vs 100

Bahrain will host the opening round of the season on March 14, which will also feature a sprint, while Abu Dhabi will stage the finale on December 12.

Australia, Japan, Canada, Great Britain, Italy, Brazil and Qatar make up the remaining sprint venues.

Portugal will return to the calendar on June 20 and Türkiye on Oct. 3, while the Barcelona-Catalunya Grand Prix and Dutch Grand Prix at Zandvoort will drop off the schedule.

Barcelona is due to return in 2028 as part of a rotation with the Belgian Grand Prix at Spa-Francorchamps.

Information from PA contributed to this report.

stories.headline: Tracking WNBA MVP race, awards: Time to vote for the winners
stories.summary: A'ja Wilson (MVP) and Olivia Miles (ROY) are shoo-ins. A Golden State duo is among our other award winners.
stories.byline: Michael Voepel and Alexa Philippou and Kendra Andrews and Kareem Copeland
stories.body:
With four days remaining in the regular season -- and official ballots due Friday -- it's time to vote on this year's WNBA awards.

Throughout the 2026 campaign, ESPN has tracked the front-runners and top contenders for MVP, Rookie of the Year, Defensive Player of the Year, Most Improved Player, Sixth Player of the Year and Coach of the Year. Now, Michael Voepel, Alexa Philippou, Kendra Andrews and Kareem Copeland make their final selections.

Among our panel, there's little intrigue for the league's biggest honor: A'ja Wilson looks poised to win her fifth MVP and fourth in five years, adding to her already-record-setting haul. Even less of a debate was ESPN's pick for Rookie of the Year, Minnesota Lynx star Olivia Miles, who also is our runner-up for MVP.

Here's where we also land on the rest of the league's top awards.

Jump to:

MVP | Rookie of Year | Defensive Player of Year

Most Improved | Sixth Player | Coach of Year

MVP

Kendra Andrews: A'ja Wilson, Las Vegas Aces

Kareem Copeland: A'ja Wilson, Las Vegas Aces

Alexa Philippou: A'ja Wilson, Las Vegas Aces

Michael Voepel: A'ja Wilson, Las Vegas Aces

ESPN's pick: A'ja Wilson, Las Vegas Aces

Last season, Wilson became the WNBA's first four-time MVP. If she wins a fifth MVP, she'll enter even more rarified air in American professional team sports history.

The all-time leader in MVP awards in the NHL is Wayne Gretzky, who won the Hart Trophy nine times, including eight in a row. Barry Bonds (seven) leads MLB players, Kareem Abdul-Jabbar (six) leads the NBA and Peyton Manning (five) leads the NFL.

Wilson's Aces are the defending WNBA champions. They are seeking their fourth title, and Wilson has been at the heart of it all since being drafted No. 1 in 2018. This season, she leads the WNBA in scoring (26.1 points per game), blocks (2.0 per game), player efficiency rating (32.4) and win shares (8.6). She ranks fourth in rebounding (9.3 per game).

Wilson, who turned 30 in August, has dealt with back issues this season that kept her from playing in the FIBA World Cup. But overall, she has remained a dominant force in the league. That's even more impressive when you consider the challengers for this award during Wilson's career, including this season. -- Voepel

ESPN's runner-up: Olivia Miles, Minnesota Lynx

You could take your pick of strong contenders, including the Indiana Fever's Caitlin Clark and Kelsey Mitchell, the New York Liberty's Breanna Stewart and the Atlanta Dream's Rhyne Howard. The case for Miles: The point guard took the keys to the Lynx's offense as a rookie with superstar forward Napheesa Collier out injured until July 22. Miles is averaging 19.8 points, 6.0 assists and 4.7 rebounds for the Lynx, who have the league's best record. Candace Parker was the only rookie to also win the WNBA's MVP award, in 2008, so it says something for a first-year player to even be in the conversation. -- Voepel

Rookie of the Year

Andrews: Olivia Miles, Minnesota Lynx

Copeland: Olivia Miles, Minnesota Lynx

Philippou: Olivia Miles, Minnesota Lynx

Voepel: Olivia Miles, Minnesota Lynx

ESPN's pick: Olivia Miles, Minnesota Lynx

From day one, Miles grabbed the lead for Rookie of the Year and never let go. In her debut, she dropped 21 points, eight assists, three rebounds and two steals -- and immediately proved she would be a force in the league. The No. 2 draft pick set the WNBA record for points scored by a rookie, and she is in the conversation to be named MVP.

Miles has been the best player on the best team throughout the season and ranks in the top 10 in the league in points and assists per game while being in the top five for rebounds per game by a guard. On Friday, Miles registered her seventh game of 20 points, five assists and five rebounds; that passed Tamika Catchings for the second most by a rookie in WNBA history and only trails Caitlin Clark (14).

Miles won every Rookie of the Month Award given by the league this season. In July, she became the 10th player in league history to record 30-plus points, eight-plus assists and eight-plus rebounds in a single game. Miles -- so dominant that we aren't even selecting a runner-up -- was instantly one of the best passers and quickly showed the ability to get to the rim at will. Defenders learned over the course of the campaign that she also can shoot from behind the arc; her eight treys on June 4 set a league record for rookies. -- Copeland

Defensive Player of the Year

Andrews: Gabby Williams, Golden State Valkyries

Copeland: Gabby Williams, Golden State Valkyries

Philippou: Gabby Williams, Golden State Valkyries

Voepel: Angel Reese, Atlanta Dream

ESPN's pick: Gabby Williams, Golden State Valkyries

The Valkyries have been the WNBA's best defensive team this season, allowing 74.8 PPG. They are the only team holding foes to fewer than 80 PPG, and opponents have shot just 41.5% from the field against them. Williams, in her first season with Golden State, has been one of the biggest keys to that effort.

The 5-foot-11 forward can guard players of all sizes. She is second in defensive rating (99.1) and one of four Valkyries players who are in the top five in that category. Williams and guard Veronica Burton, also a candidate for this award, lead the Valkyries in averaging 1.6 steals apiece. -- Voepel

ESPN's runner-up: Angel Reese, Atlanta Dream

Atlanta is second to Golden State in defensive rating (104.9), and Reese has improved her defense enough in her third WNBA season to be considered for this award. At 6-foot-4, she is a strong post defender and an elite rebounder who also can guard on the perimeter and cut off passing lanes. Reese leads the WNBA in defensive win shares (3.2) and is fourth in defensive rating (100.4).

Wilson, a three-time WNBA DPOY, is also in contention for this honor. -- Voepel

Most Improved Player

Andrews: Jessica Shepard, Dallas Wings

Copeland: Shakira Austin, Washington Mystics

Philippou: Jessica Shepard, Dallas Wings

Voepel: Jessica Shepard, Dallas Wings

ESPN's pick: Jessica Shepard, Dallas Wings

Players tend to end up in the Most Improved conversation in a few different ways. They might finally be healthy, enjoying an expanded role, thriving in a new system or benefitting from the work they put into the offseason. Shepard's successful campaign is largely a product of having more opportunity with the Wings; her 31.6 minutes per game are a career high and 10 more than she averaged last year with Minnesota. But even in her best stretches with the Lynx, it wasn't obvious she'd one day become such a critical, go-to player who a playoff-bound team -- and, in the longer term, a championship-minded one -- can build around and play through.

Shepard is on track to become the first player to average at least 10 points, 10 rebounds and five assists in a season. (Candace Parker did so in 2015, but in only 16 games.) And while Alyssa Thomas is still the league's triple-double queen, Shepard leads the WNBA this season in that category with five. And Shepard's 23 double-doubles are second most, behind Angel Reese. That's all from a second-round draft pick who turned 30 this year and never averaged more than 8.1 points per game prior to this season. -- Philippou

ESPN's runner-up: Shakira Austin, Washington Mystics

Austin has been known for her defense and athleticism since entering the league, but her offensive game took a significant step forward as she helped the Mystics return to the playoffs for the first time since 2023. Her scoring average has increased by more than four points over that of last year to rank in the top 15 in the league, and she has averaged three more rebounds to rank in the top five.

Finally healthy, Austin has displayed an expanded offensive repertoire with an ability to put the ball on the floor and attack from the perimeter with her 6-foot-5 frame. The No. 3 draft pick in 2023 ranks in the top 11 in defensive win shares for the No. 2 scoring defense in the league. -- Copeland

Sixth Player of the Year

Andrews: Janelle Salaun, Golden State Valkyries

Copeland: Janelle Salaun, Golden State Valkyries

Philippou: Janelle Salaun, Golden State Valkyries

Voepel: Janelle Salaun, Golden State Valkyries

ESPN's pick: Janelle Salaun, Golden State Valkyries

Few players have provided as big a spark off the bench as Salaun has for Golden State. In 22.9 minutes per game, she has become the team's second-best scorer, averaging 12.9 points. That's also the second-best scoring mark in the league among bench players seeing at least 20 minutes per game.

Salaun has established herself as one of the premier knockdown shooters in the WNBA, shooting 39.7% from 3 on 6.1 attempts per game, which is the best percentage among bench players averaging at least five 3-point shots.

The Valkyries outscore opponents by 4.7 points when Salaun is on the floor -- the second-best net rating among bench players averaging at least 20 minutes -- as she has made a habit of providing momentum-shifting plays. -- Andrews

ESPN's runner-up: Marine Johannes, New York Liberty

Johannes started for New York early on, but she has come off the bench in all but two games since June 19. She has been one of the Liberty's most dependable reserves, averaging 8.7 points, 2.1 rebounds and 2.4 assists. -- Voepel

Coach of the Year

Andrews: Cheryl Reeve, Minnesota Lynx

Copeland: Cheryl Reeve, Minnesota Lynx

Philippou: Cheryl Reeve, Minnesota Lynx

Voepel: Cheryl Reeve, Minnesota Lynx

ESPN's pick: Cheryl Reeve, Minnesota Lynx

The Lynx have been a regular-season powerhouse for several consecutive years, but what Reeve has led them to this season feels different. Without Collier, their superstar forward, for much of the year, Reeve has coached rookie sensation Miles into one of the best and most impactful players in the league and established a new identity with a roster that started the campaign with just two returning players.

The Lynx have had the league's best record all season and are trying to clinch the No. 1 seed heading into the playoffs. They have the third-best offense (112.5 offensive rating) and the third-best defense (103.7 defensive rating).

In July, Collier told ESPN that if this season has proved anything, it's to never count out Reeve. Yes, she is the all-time winningest coach in league history, but remember that entering this season, some questioned how Minnesota would stay afloat with so much roster turnover and Collier sidelined indefinitely. Reeve has overachieved, outperformed expectations and once again led Minnesota to be a top contender. -- Andrews

ESPN's runner-up: Sydney Johnson, Washington Mystics

The Mystics were supposed to be in a methodical rebuild with a new draft-and-develop strategy that could take some time to return to the postseason. In Year 2, Johnson led Washington to the playoffs as the youngest team in league history to make the postseason. With six first-round picks from the past two drafts, Johnson has molded Washington into a defensive force as the No. 2 scoring defense in the league. He adapted when the big three of Austin, Kiki Iriafen and Sonia Citron requested that Johnson be more demanding, and he put more of an emphasis on wins and losses after 2025 was focused on building a cultural foundation. The Mystics' 26 wins this season matches that of their 2019 WNBA championship team for the most in franchise history. Washington is back in the playoffs for the first time since 2023. -- Copeland

stories.headline: MLS Power Rankings: Union skyrocket as unbeaten streak reaches 11 games
stories.summary: Can anyone stop the Philadelphia Union? Their latest win powered them up the charts in this week's edition of ESPN's MLS Power Rankings.
stories.body:
It's Monday, another weekend of action is in the books, and it's time for the latest edition of ESPN's MLS Power Rankings.

1. Nashville SC
Previous ranking: 1

In one of the most important matches of their end-of-season schedule, Sam Surridge scored in the fourth and 91st minutes to help secure a 2-2 draw against Miami. With the point, Nashville is winless in three (two draws, one defeat) but still in a position to break Inter's Supporters' Shield record with nine games to go.

2. St. Louis City SC
Previous ranking: 2

Nashville further tightened their grip on the Supporters' Shield with a 3-0 win over Chicago on Saturday. A dominant first-half display mixed with some savvy transition attacking in the second half saw all three of the club's designated players find the back of the net.

3. Vancouver Whitecaps
Previous ranking: 3

The Whitecaps took care of business against Salt Lake by a 3-0 scoreline, thoroughly outplaying their hosts. Few teams in the league can match Vancouver for attacking difference-makers, with summer signing Yadaly Diaby making his first league start and notching two goal contributions.

4. Inter Miami CF
Previous ranking: 4

Inching closer to full health, star left back Sergio Reguilón saw the field in the second half as Miami played to a 2-2 draw with San Diego. While the attack still lacks balance without a threat coming down the wings, even a partially hampered Inter Miami squad still boasts some of the sport's best-ever attackers. Lionel Messi and Luis Suárez both found the back of the net Sunday.

5. New England Revolution
Previous ranking: 8

Riding the high of his first call-up to the U.S. men's national team, Peyton Miller bagged a brace in the Revolution's 4-2 victory over Orlando on Saturday. With his sizzling speed and developing goal threat, the 18-year-old did well to help lead New England in the absence of the injured Jack Harrison.

6. Philadelphia Union
Previous ranking: 13

Can anyone stop the Union? Despite falling into a three-goal hole on the road in Kansas City, Philadelphia scored four goals in a nine-minute span in the second half to claim a 4-3 win. They've now gone 11 straight games without a loss in league play.

7. LAFC
Previous ranking: 6

Despite taking a 2-0 lead over San Jose in the California Clásico, a 10-man LAFC couldn't hold on for all three points against their in-state rivals. Two second-half concessions, including one late in stoppage time, turned three points into one in a 2-2 draw.

8. Charlotte FC
Previous ranking: 11

Allan Saint-Maximin opened his Charlotte account with a goal in a 2-1 victory over D.C. United on Saturday. If coach Dean Smith can tap into the former Newcastle man's one-on-one dribbling and his goal threat, Charlotte FC will be a difficult postseason out.

9. Houston Dynamo
Previous ranking: 10

For more than 45 minutes of action, it looked as if Mateusz Bogusz's penalty conversion had sealed a win for the Dynamo over Cincinnati. However, late in second-half stoppage time, the Polish attacker conceded a penalty that allowed the visitors to equalize at 2-2.

10. Orlando City
Previous ranking: 12

Missing Antoine Griezmann because of a thigh injury suffered in their midweek U.S. Open Cup semifinal defeat, Orlando fell 4-2 to New England. Outside of Lionel Messi, there might not be a player more important to his team's trophy chances than the Frenchman.

11. Chicago Fire
Previous ranking: 9

A 3-0 loss to Nashville marked seven straight games across all competitions for the Fire without a win. While Robert Lewandowski's scoring record has been positive since he arrived in MLS, it looks as if Chicago's major shift up top has destabilized so much of what propelled them in the spring.

12. New York City FC
Previous ranking: 7

Life has been a slog for New York City lately. A series of poor results over the past two months was extended to include a 1-0 defeat Friday at the hands of their biggest rivals: Red Bull New York. While they created enough chances to win, conversion in front of goal lagged for NYCFC.

13. FC Cincinnati
Previous ranking: 5

Cincinnati left it late but managed to earn a 2-2 road draw against the Dynamo. Kévin Denkey's penalty in the 97th minute rescued the trip, though that doesn't change the fact that Pat Noonan's team has gone five games without a victory.

14. FC Dallas
Previous ranking: 14

After three consecutive victories before this weekend, Dallas played Austin to a 0-0 draw Saturday. Though they created the better chances, Brad Stuver's impressive goalkeeping limited the home side to a solitary point.

15. LA Galaxy
Previous ranking: 17

It was hardly a dominant showing from the Galaxy, but Greg Vanney's team managed a comeback 3-2 victory on the road in Minnesota, with a makeshift front line that featured Chucky Lozano playing underneath the striker and fullback Harbor Miller back in the attack. Still, all three points count the same.

16. San Diego FC
Previous ranking: 16

Thanks to a brace from Anders Dreyer, San Diego earned a 2-2 draw with Miami on Sunday night. While the sophomore outfit still sits below the playoff line out West, they only trail the ninth-placed Portland Timbers by a single point.

17. San Jose Earthquakes
Previous ranking: 21

Though their summer slide saw San Jose tumble down these rankings, things have stabilized for the Quakes. Their 2-2 draw with LAFC on Saturday marked five straight results, and Timo Werner's return from injury made the outing all the brighter.

18. Real Salt Lake
Previous ranking: 15

Salt Lake were never truly in their match against Vancouver, allowing two goals in the first 30 minutes and failing to ever mount a convincing attack. With Diego Luna now expected to miss the rest of the season with a knee injury, RSL's path to contention is murkier than at any prior point in the season.

19. Red Bull New York
Previous ranking: 20

Between his call-up to the U.S. men's national team and his goal to cap off a 1-0 win for Red Bull New York in the Hudson River derby against New York City, Julian Hall has had quite the week. Along the way, Michael Bradley's team defended well for much of Friday's game, which hasn't always been true of them in 2026.

20. Seattle Sounders
Previous ranking: 22

The Sounders' summer signings helped rescue a 3-3 draw in Colorado, with Dejan Joveljić and Caden Clark each nabbing a goal to see their new outfit equalize in Colorado. For a team that's still dealing with a slew of injuries, every point is crucial.

21. Austin FC
Previous ranking: 25

Don't look now, but Austin have managed seven straight results in league play. Most recently, they held Dallas to a scoreless draw thanks to some impressive goalkeeping and possession control. It's not flashy, but there's momentum building for 2027.

22. Colorado Rapids
Previous ranking: 27

The good? New winger Morgan Whittaker scored a brace in his first MLS start and looks the part of a superstar. The bad? The Rapids blew a multigoal lead to draw 3-3 at home with Seattle.

23. Columbus Crew
Previous ranking: 26

Laurent Courtois' return to Montréal went as well as the interim manager could've hoped. His Columbus team dispatched their hosts -- who double as the Frenchman's former employer -- by a 2-0 scoreline.

24. Minnesota United
Previous ranking: 18

Minnesota have dropped points from winning or even positions in each of their past five games, including Saturday's 3-2 home loss to the Galaxy. It's safe to say things have gone off the rails for the Loons.

25. Toronto FC
Previous ranking: 19

Every now and then, you come up against a team that puts you in your place. That's what happened for Toronto in their 3-1 loss to St. Louis. There's still a distance for Toronto to go before they're on the level of MLS's best.

26. Portland Timbers
Previous ranking: 24

The Timbers put up a valiant late-game effort and scored in the 93rd minute, but it wasn't enough to salvage a point in Texas as they stumbled to a 2-1 defeat to Dallas.

27. D.C. United
Previous ranking: 23

While they largely outplayed Charlotte, D.C. still fell 2-1. Even when the team plays well, results still aren't trickling into the nation's capital. D.C. United have just six wins this season, one more than bottom-feeders Montréal and Kansas City.

28. Atlanta United
Previous ranking: 28

There haven't been as many moments of Aleksei Miranchuk magic as Atlanta would've hoped for when they signed him from Atalanta, but the playmaker delivered Saturday. His goal made the difference in the Five Stripes' 1-0 road win over the Timbers.

29. Sporting Kansas City
Previous ranking: 29

What looked destined to be a second straight impressive victory for Kansas City turned into a disaster when the hosts conceded four goals in less than 10 minutes to Philadelphia to lose 4-3 on Saturday. Still, André Luiz dominating in the attack after joining this summer is a silver lining.

30. CF Montréal
Previous ranking: 30

Up against their old head coach, Courtois, Montréal fell 2-0 at home to the Crew. At least they're through to the Canadian Championship final?

stories.headline: Small changes in biggest weight class in MMA divisional rankings
stories.summary: Here's a look at every weight class to determine the best of the best in UFC, PFL and beyond.
stories.body:
The UFC's heavyweight division appears to be stuck in neutral gear.

It's not just about Tom Aspinall vacating the championship on Monday because he is still recovering from an eye injury suffered in last October's no-contest in a title defense against Ciryl Gane. Gane, who won the interim championship with a knockout of Alex Pereira in June, remains atop the ESPN rankings. The top 10 still features Aspinall -- he's eligible to be ranked until the middle of next month, when he will have been inactive for a year -- and includes two heavyweights from outside the UFC in the top six (Francis Ngannou, Vadim Nemkov).

The heavyweight rankings underwent small changes as a result of Saturday's UFC matchup of top-10 fighters Waldo Cortes Acosta and Curtis Blaydes. Cortes Acosta entered the weekend ranked sixth, but after losing by unanimous decision, he drops to No. 9. Blaydes is one spot above him, moving up from 10th.

The only other movement in the divisional rankings is at women's flyweight, where former UFC champion Alexa Grasso moves up one position to No. 4 after Saturday's unanimous decision win over Manon Fiorot. Formerly ranked second, Fiorot drops three spots after her first loss in a nontitle bout since her pro debut in 2018.

Here are the ESPN pound-for-pound MMA rankings and a list of current UFC champions in all weight classes.

Results are current; rankings as of Sept. 15. To be eligible for the rankings, a fighter must have competed over the past 12 months or must have an upcoming fight booked. Fighters who have been dropped for inactivity can be reinstated only after they compete.

stories.headline: Harry Maguire: Man United didn't take chances against Fulham, paid the price
stories.summary: Harry Maguire said Manchester United paid the price for failing to take their chances in Sunday's 1-1 draw against Fulham.
stories.body:
Harry Maguire said Manchester United paid the price for failing to take their chances in Sunday's 1-1 draw against Fulham.

United were fortunate to leave west London with a point after Matheus Cunha's late deflected goal deceived goalkeeper Bernd Leno and denied Alvaro Arbeloa a first Premier League win in charge.

Sky Sports pundit Gary Neville branded the first 15 minutes of the second half, which culminated in a comical own goal from Lisandro Martínez to put Fulham in front, the worst he had seen in more than 45 years of watching the team play.

United hit a post in the first half through Bruno Fernandes, while Leno produced fine saves from Cunha, Martinez and Bryan Mbeumo.

"We have got to take our chances and take our moments," Maguire said to club media. "When you come away in the Premier League it is tough and you have seen that in the results this year.

"When we had those moments in that first half, they are big moments in the Premier League and you have really got to take them."

Fulham's goal went down against Martinez's name, but the blame was shared with his goalkeeper, a botched effort by Senne Lammens to shovel away Calvin Bassey's shot with his legs rather than his gloves, then an equally inexplicable and muddled attempt at keeping the defender's pass back to him out of his net.

The result means United have collected their joint fewest number of points after five matches in Premier League history.

Not since the 2014-15 season under Lous van Gaal have United picked up only five points by this stage and Carrick's class of 2026 will spend the extended international break in the bottom half of the table.

The team 11 years ago recovered from their poor start to eventually finish fourth and Maguire believes the current crop can kick on despite more dropped points.

"Our reaction was so much better and positive than it was last week [against Manchester City] and to concede that goal with the week we have had, the boys showed great spirit and great reaction," he said.

"We pushed them right back and the pressure was relentless. We needed a ball to fall or drop for us.

"It was just unfortunate that the goal did not come earlier as we had the momentum to go and win the match."

- Carrick has an impossible job at Man United after transfer failures

- Michael Carrick keen to find Man United positives, but there aren't many right now

- Carrick quashes notion Manchester United are out of shape

Cunha's 89th-minute shot hit defender David Affengruber and span cruelly past the wrong-footed Leno, with Fulham just minutes from victory.

It was, however, a muted, lethargic display from Carrick's team, who are now three league matches without a victory.

But Maguire said: "You have got to ignore the noise and really believe and think about what we have done this year, along with what we need to work on and improve on, but we are not far away."

stories.headline: Fantasy baseball news: Yesavage returns as Toronto seeks a late-season miracle
stories.summary: All of the important fantasy spin and actionable takeaways resulting from the latest baseball news.
stories.body:
Everything that happens in and around MLB has some additional context when viewed from a fantasy baseball perspective. From lineup changes to minor league call-ups to injuries and so much more, the news cycle will constantly affect player values in fantasy baseball.

Our fantasy baseball buzz file, with contributions from our ESPN fantasy writers, aims to provide fantasy managers with the intel they need as news breaks around MLB.

Sept. 21: Monday's news to know
By Todd Zola

The final Monday of the regular season features only three games -- all evening affairs -- beginning at 6:35 p.m. ET with the Toronto Blue Jays visiting the Baltimore Orioles. A few minutes later, the Detroit Tigers host the Washington Nationals. The San Francisco Giants entertain the Minnesota Twins, closing out the truncated slate, at 9:45 p.m. ET.

Three teams have clinched a postseason berth in the American League -- all from the East. The Tampa Bay Rays are on the cusp of securing the division, with the New York Yankees and Boston Red Sox ticketed to run back their 2025 wild-card matchup in the Bronx.
The Cleveland Guardians lead the Chicago White Sox by one game in the AL Central. The second-place finisher would be in the driver's seat for the final wild card. In the West, the Texas Rangers are one game up on the Houston Astros. The second-place finisher still has an outside chance at the last wild-card spot.
All three National League divisions have been clinched, with the Atlanta Braves ruling the East, the Milwaukee Brewers sitting atop the Central, and the Los Angeles Dodgers having nailed down the West. The Brewers have a two-game lead over the Dodgers for the best record in the Senior Circuit. The seedings for the Wild Card Series could go down to the end, with the Philadelphia Phillies just one game behind the Chicago Cubs and San Diego Padres. The Arizona Diamondbacks have not yet been eliminated, but they're four games behind the Phillies and a lot has to happen for them to extend their season.
The Blue Jays are set to activate Trey Yesavage from the 15-day IL to start tonight's road affair against the Orioles, but they're aiming for only 45-60 pitches from the 23-year-old right-hander. He has been sidelined following meniscus surgery on his right knee and made only one rehab start, recording just two outs in that effort. The rest of the game will be a bullpen affair.
River Ryan is poised to make his first MLB appearance since 2024. He was acquired by the Tigers in the Tarik Skubal deal. The 28-year-old right-hander was shelved by a hamstring injury at the time but recently made two rehab starts for Triple-A Toledo. He'll handle a few innings before tagging in Keider Montero as the primary pitcher.
The Nationals will counter with DJ Herz, who has been recovering from April 2025 Tommy John surgery. The 25-year-old lefty threw 20 2/3 innings in rehab, the last 13 with Triple-A Rochester. He worked up to 65 pitches, so Herz could manage at least five frames if he's sharp.
Bryce Eldridge of the Giants has not been placed on the 7-day IL, but he nevertheless remains in the league's concussion protocol. The rookie is unlikely to play tonight against the Twins.

Be sure to check out the latest fantasy lineup advice as well as the MLB betting tips for Monday.

Sept. 20: Sunday's news to know

By Todd Zola

The penultimate Sunday of the regular season gets going at 1:10 p.m. ET with the New York Mets hosting the Philadelphia Phillies. This is one of a few contests that may have to deal with rain. Both clubs have Monday off, howver, if conditions prohibit playing the game and there's a need to reschedule.

Other matchups under any kind of "weather watch" include the Pittsburgh Pirates at the Kansas City Royals, the Athletics at the Cleveland Guardians and the Detroit Tigers at the Chicago White Sox. Fortunately, none of these six teams are slated to play on Monday either, so the same "wiggle room" applies.
The Boston Red Sox are rearranging their rotation to line up for their likely wild-card series. This pushes Payton Tolle to Tuesday, with Patrick Sandoval taking the hill this afternoon in the rubber game against the Tampa Bay Rays.
Bryce Eldridge is in the league's concussion protocol and will miss today's NL West matchup between the San Francisco Giants and Los Angeles Dodgers. He reportedly bumped his head at the team hotel. Brett Harris will likely fill in at first base.
Kyle Tucker left yesterday's contest in the seventh inning after fouling a ball off his leg. The Dodgers were ahead by six runs at the time and manager Dave Roberts indicated that the score helped in the decision. He's hopeful that the outfielder will play today. It's been a frustrating year for Tucker, but he's doing his best to salvage the season with a .327/.424/.796 line over his last 15 games.

stories.headline: Collingwood star Nick Daicos wins 2026 Brownlow Medal
stories.summary: Collingwood superstar Nick Daicos has finally claimed his first Brownlow Medal in a runaway victory with a record-breaking 47 votes.
stories.body:
Collingwood superstar Nick Daicos has finally claimed his first Brownlow Medal in a runaway victory with a record-breaking 47 votes.

The 23-year-old surged to a perfect nine votes from his first three games, led from round 11, then registered six consecutive best-on-ground performances to seal victory by round 21.

Daicos won the AFL's greatest individual honour from Western Bulldogs champion and three-time runner-up Marcus Bontempelli (34) and Geelong star Bailey Smith (33).

The Magpie had 13 three-vote performances and beat the previous votes record of 45 set by Carlton champion Patrick Cripps in 2024.

Daicos, the son of Magpies great Peter Daicos, finally prevailed after runner-up finishes in the past two seasons, a third placing in 2023 and an eighth place in his debut year of 2022.

The dynamic midfielder had already snared the AFL Players Association and AFL Coaches Association player-of-the-year awards this season.

It was the fourth consecutive year that Daicos was favourite, and with the umpires able to consult statistics for the first time, the star Magpie was irresistible.

Daicos averaged 34.9 disposals, 5.7 clearances, 6.7 inside-50s and 1.1 goals.

The brilliant playmaker was edged out by Gold Coast's Matt Rowell last year and Cripps the year before, when Daicos polled 38 votes.

The Collingwood vice-captain - widely expected to be named the club's skipper next season - is the club's first Brownlow medallist since Dane Swan in 2011.

Sydney stars Isaac Heeney and Chad Warner weren't in the room as they polled 26 and 12 votes respectively.

The pair were among five Swans stood down by Sydney for breaching club standards and weren't invited to the Brownlow function at Crown Palladium, but remained eligible for the award.

Separately, a police investigation into sexual assault allegations related to what allegedly took place in a room at East Melbourne's Pullman Hotel in August is ongoing.

Brisbane's Conor McKenna won goal of the year while Hawthorn dynamo Nick Watson was awarded mark of the year.

stories.headline: Greg Wyshynski's 'Plant my flag' list: Celebrini, Schaefer and players to take in every league
stories.summary: Greg Wyshynski is back with the 10 players he's looking to draft in every 2026 fantasy hockey league.
stories.body:
The start of the NHL regular season always arrives with a jolt of unfettered optimism. Many teams have Stanley Cup aspirations; those that do not will hopefully give fans something to be optimistic about for the future.

The start of fantasy hockey brings the same emotions. Players are projected to do great things, they are ranked based on that projection, and then we select them for our fantasy franchises with the optimism that they'll hit their statistical marks.

Until, of course, they don't and we're left making desperation trade proposals to our friends and scouring the waiver wire hoping to find an overlooked diamond in the ice shavings.

It doesn't have to be this way. There are players this season who should deliver the goods -- and, in some cases, level up even higher than their draft rankings would indicate. The 10 players discussed here are the ones on whom I plant my rhetorical flag for the 2026-27 NHL season. Some are the best of the best. Others are consistent contributors. A few are selections that will either make me look very smart or very stupid in my drafting prowess.

My selections are based on how I believe the players will perform this season and how they'll rack up the points in ESPN Fantasy standard scoring:

Skaters: goals = 2 points; assists = 1 point; shots and hits = 0.1 points; blocked shots and special teams points = 0.5 points.
Goaltenders: wins = 4 points; OT losses = 1 point; shutouts = 3 points; saves = 0.2 points; goals against = -2 points.

Here's the Plant My Flag list for 2026-27. May all your picks turn out to be great ones.

More: Sign up for free | Rankings | Projections | League types

Macklin Celebrini, C, San Jose Sharks

There are essentially the same seven players at the top of every fantasy rankings list this season. Nathan MacKinnon and Connor McDavid are either first or second overall. Nikita Kucherov, Leon Draisaitl and David Pastrnak are right behind them. Cale Makar is the token nonforward, as the best defenseman on the planet.

And then there's the 20-year-old kid from San Jose that has played himself into this rarified company. Celebrini had 115 points, including 45 goals, in his second NHL season to finish fourth in the MVP balloting. He had 33 power-play points. He began to earn Sidney Crosby comparisons, but even Sid the Kid didn't rifle the puck 287 times in 82 games as an NHL sophomore like Celebrini did.

I think Celebrini levels up again this season, not only because he'll continue to figure out the pro game but because the Sharks overall should be improved year over year. Most rankings and league drafts that I've seen had Celebrini around fourth overall. By the end of the season, we might be wondering how he wasn't everyone's top choice. He's that good.

Matthew Schaefer, D, New York Islanders

Look, putting Schaefer on your fantasy team is worth it for the vibes alone. His puppy-dog comportment will liven up your fantasy hockey locker room, and his boundless enthusiasm will reinvigorate the crusty veterans who drag their tired bodies onto the fantasy ice on a random winter Tuesday night to earn you 0.1 points with a hit.

But last season's Calder Trophy winner is more than vibes. He's projecting to be an incredibly valuable fantasy point producer, at least in ESPN standard scoring. Schaefer had 59 points in 82 games last season. That was with 18 power-play points, so even a reasonable improvement there could push him to 70 points this season.

What I love about Schaefer's offense is his goal scoring from the back end. His 23 goals last season were the most for a rookie defenseman since Brian Leetch scored 23 with the New York Rangers in 1988-89.

But the real tantalizing part of his game from a fantasy perspective is his shot blocking. (Again, depending on how your league is scored.) Schaefer had 111 blocked shots last season to lead all rookies. Barring some fundamental change in his game encouraged by coach Peter DeBoer, Schaefer is going to hit that sweet spot of offensive pop and defensive fantasy stats. Now we just need ESPN Fantasy to hand out points for vibes.

Filip Forsberg, F, Nashville Predators

The 32-year-old Forsberg offers something I value in my fantasy drafting: The known quantity who could level up, depending on how well the young talent around him plays. Forsberg is a model of consistency. He has played 82 games in three straight seasons. He crested over 40 goals in two of those seasons, including a 94-point campaign in 2023-24 that remains his career apex. He has been in double digits in power-play goals in all three seasons. He shoots the puck a bunch, throws the body a ton, with at least 124 hits in each of the past three seasons, and he'll also block a shot or two.

Word out of Nashville in the preseason is that Forsberg has been working with 21-year-old winger Matthew Wood, who had an impressive rookie season with 17 goals in 71 games despite skating just 12:19 per game. They worked well together in limited time as linemates last season, enough to pique my interest about Forsberg increasing his point total (75) from 2025-26. But even if he's just the Forsberg we've seen over the past three seasons, that's still an incredibly valuable fantasy player.

Brady Tkachuk, LW, Florida Panthers

The two best lines of the preseason for the Panthers:

The line coach Paul Maurice had when asked if Brady and Matthew Tkachuk might flank center Sam Bennett on what would be the NHL's most bludgeoning trio: "I don't want to give everybody what they want with the two Tkachuk brothers together with Sam Bennett in the middle. They'll be in jail before the puck drops." Great stuff.
The line that Brady Tkachuk, acquired by Florida from the Ottawa Senators in the summer, will likely start this season on. He's expected to have Aleksander Barkov in the middle, who missed all last season with a right knee injury; and Sam Reinhart on his wing, a player two years removed from a 57-goal season.

Brady Tkachuk was a consistent offensive force in the regular season during his eight seasons in Ottawa. While limited to 60 games last season, he put up the best points per 60 minutes mark (3.5) of his career.

I am a little concerned about how his numbers will look as he goes from the fulcrum of the Ottawa offense to a cog in the Panthers' machine. Will he keep his elephantine shots on goal averages, playing on a line with Reinhart or (potentially and perhaps inevitably) his brother Matthew? That's a mystery.

What can't be denied is Brady's motivation to stifle his critics (especially up north), make up for his disappearing act offensively in last postseason and make a strong impression with his new team. There's no room at the Elbo Room in Fort Lauderdale for an underachiever.

John Carlson, D, Tampa Bay Lightning

Carlson turns 37 next January, so this is conceivably the last time I'll ever plant my flag on this particular defenseman. If that's the case, what a last fantasy hockey hurrah it'll be for Carlson, as the quarterback of the Tampa Bay power play.

He's essentially the replacement for Darren Raddysh, who had 10 goals and 16 helpers on the man advantage in a breakout season that led to him getting eight years and $68 million from the Toronto Maple Leafs. Raddysh put up those numbers on a power play that ranked in the middle of the pack, thanks in large part to a slew of man games lost to key offensive players like Brayden Point (63 games played).

Carlson split time between the Washington Capitals and the Anaheim Ducks, who acquired him at the trade deadline. He had 60 points in 71 games, his best offensive season since 2021-22, but earned only 14 points on the power play, which is what happens when you're QB1 for the 23rd (Anaheim) and 25th (Washington, inexplicably) teams in the league on the man advantage, respectively.

What really intrigues me about Carlson on the Lightning power play is that he's a quarterback in name only. The power play runs through Nikita Kucherov, or the "maestro" as GM Julien BriseBois called him. A right-shot defenseman like Carlson is ideal for that kind of setup, as Kucherov distributes the puck from the right wing.

I don't know if Carlson is getting to 10 power-play goals like Raddysh last season -- his career high is seven -- but I do think we'll see a substantial power-play stat impact to go along with his consistent 5-on-5 output.

Wyatt Johnston, C, Dallas Stars

Should a player that has scored 110 goals over the past three seasons combined -- including 45 tallies in 2025-26 -- have an average draft position of around 20th and be ranked 26th on the ESPN fantasy list? He should probably be higher, but my fellow Wyatt Johnston fans don't mind seeing this absolute sure thing slip down the draft board.

If the question is why a guy who scores goals and sees copious amounts of ice time with Mikko Rantanen and Jason Robertson might not rank inside the top 20, the answer might be how Johnston hit that career high of 45 goals last season. He jumped from 11 goals to 27 goals on a power play that ranked second in the NHL. Maybe some fantasy users are skeptical he could do that again, or that the power play will be as effective.

First, it's important to note that the power play leveled up thanks to coach Neil Graham, the former Texas Stars bench boss who was put in charge of that unit in Dallas. His incredible preparation and prescouting allowed the Stars to exploit opposing penalty kills, and I imagine that'll continue this season. Second, all the players who made that power play sing are back as well.

Johnston, 23, saw a slight dip in his even-strength production last season and still posted 18 goals and 26 assists. He's a player with levels yet reached. I just wish he shot the puck a little more often.

ESPN Fantasy Hockey is the fun, free way to get inside the game. Draft your players, set your lineups and earn points when the pros do. Sign up today!

Jet Greaves, G, Columbus Blue Jackets

The NHL's goaltenders are split up into two groups for fantasy hockey: The every-night starters and the tandems. The latter requires a bit more attention to ensure you're starting the guy who is actually playing that night. The former is more "set it and forget it." The problem is that the NHL has trended toward tandems for the better part of this decade. Only 12 goalies last season earned at least 65% of the crease time on their teams.

One of those goalies was the 25-year-old Greaves, who had a breakout season with 26 wins in 55 games and a .908 save percentage. That earned him a tidy three-year, $15 million contract extension from the Blue Jackets.

Columbus is a tricky team to figure out in the East. They went 21-11-5 under Rick Bowness after he took over as head coach and barely missed the playoffs. This offseason saw the team nearly trade its Norris Trophy-winning defenseman Zach Werenski before he blocked it with his trade protection. Things are a little weird.

Greaves, however, is a stabilizing force in goal and a player who should see his starts increase over last season. That's especially true now that goalie Elvis Merzlikins, who appeared in 30 games last season, failed his physical this week and remains out indefinitely after shoulder surgery. The team brought in 39-year-old Cam Talbot as insurance.

Greaves was ninth in goals saved above expected last season (16.5), playing behind a defense that allowed the 11th-most shots per game (28.8). ESPN has him ranked 22nd among all goalies, and I've seen him ranked around 18th in other leagues. I think he's an underrated fantasy option, and one who is going to build on last season's success.

Brandt Clarke, D, Los Angeles Kings

The Kings rewarded Clarke with a seven-year deal and a $7.4 million cap hit last summer, and there's every chance that deal is going to look like a bargain in short order. Clarke, 23, is positioned to have a breakout season for Los Angeles. His points jumped from 33 to 40 last season, as his ice time jumped from 16:17 to 19:48. He was given the reins to the Kings' top power play. He has great playmaking ability and loves jumping into the action in the offensive zone. A 10-point jump in production isn't out of the question.

But what makes Clarke a tantalizing fantasy option in ESPN leagues aren't the goals he's creating, but the ones he's preventing. He led all defensemen last season with 6.83 blocked shots per 60 minutes. No one pairs this kind of offensive upside with shot-blocking ability among defensemen. Remember: blocked shots (0.5) are worth more points than actual shots (0.1) in ESPN head-to-head leagues' standard scoring.

All Clarke needs is for new head coach Peter Laviolette to give him the ice time former coach Jim Hiller wasn't giving him.

Made it this far? Create your own league with your own rules and play against your friends today.

Dylan Holloway, F, St. Louis Blues

What's not to love here?

Holloway, aka "The one that got away" for Edmonton fans, has blossomed into a top-line scoring winger for the Blues. His goals and points per 60 minutes were consistent over the past two seasons, although his 2025-26 campaign was limited to 59 games due to a right ankle injury. He's a banging forechecker with 294 hits in his past 136 games, with 91 blocked shots in that span.

He enters this season as a member of one of the NHL's best trios with captain Robert Thomas centering Holloway and Jimmy Snuggerud, who was fifth in the Calder Trophy voting last season. They produced a ridiculous 5.7 goals per 60 minutes together in 2025-26, with an even more ridiculous 80% share of goals at even strength.

One area of concern, outside of Holloway's ability to stay in the lineup: He saw his power-play time increase last season, but his numbers didn't increase with it. He has clear 30-goal, 70-point potential but probably needs to bump those stats up to get there.

Sergei Murashov, G, Pittsburgh Penguins

Finally, every fantasy draft should include a "big maybe" with a ceiling higher than St. Patrick's Cathedral.

When the Penguins let Stuart Skinner skate away as a free agent and didn't seek another veteran stopgap in goal, it was clearly Murashov's time to stop percolating in the AHL and make the jump to the senior circuit. The anticipation in Pittsburgh has been building for him, after dominant stints in the KHL and with the Wilkes-Barre/Scranton Penguins.

The Penguins handed Arturs Silovs a one-year contract extension to allow Murashov to ease in as part of a tandem. But as ESPN's Rachel Kryshak noted: "There is a legitimate chance that Murashov is the 1A starting goaltender for the Penguins at some point this season, and if that's the case, not only is he a top prospect, but he's also probably in the Calder conversation."

All that said, he's 22 years old. There aren't many goalies that young who play as many games as Murashov will need to play to make a rookie of the year push.

Pensburgh noted that only two goalies last season who played at least 25 games were under the age of 24: Jesper Wallstedt of the Minnesota Wild and Yaroslav Askarov of the Sharks. Talk about a range of possibilities: "The Wall" was sixth for the Calder with a .915 save percentage, while Askarov had an .883 save percentage and a minus-18.9 goals saved above expected.

But that's the beauty of fantasy hockey. If Murashov takes over the crease and dominates, you were brilliant enough to draft him where you did. If he doesn't ... well, it's time to plant your flag again on the waiver wire.

stories.headline: Still at zero: Viral Man United fan's haircut challenge nears two years
stories.summary: Viral Manchester United fan Frank Ilett's haircut challenge is nearing the two-year mark and he's back to square 1.
stories.body:
For most clubs, failure or success can be defined in points, trophies and medals. Manchester United are the same, but they can also define it in days. More specifically, it can be summed up in 712 days.

That's how long viral United fan Frank Ilett, also known as The United Strand, has gone without a haircut as he waits for the team to win five games in a row.

After finishing last season with wins over Nottingham Forest and Brighton, Michael Carrick's side could have completed the job with wins over newly promoted Hull City and Ipswich Town before finishing with a win away at Everton. As it turned out, that's not at all what happened.

An embarrassing 2-0 away defeat to Hull meant going back to square one. A 5-2 win over Ipswich might have promoted hopes that the season opener was just an unwanted blip, but a draw to Everton and a controversial defeat to 10-man Manchester City poured further cold water.

How could it get worse? Well, a 2-0 lead inside the first 10 minutes against Brighton in the Carabao Cup ended in a surprise 3-2 defeat.

Left watching on, his hair growing ever longer, is Ilett. His challenge will now officially reach the two-year mark -- his last haircut was on Oct. 5, 2024 -- and his hair is now almost 14 inches at its longest point.

In the meantime, Ilett continues to raise money for the Little Princess Trust, which creates wigs for children with cancer.

The only thing that can happen now before Ilett soars past two years is for United to win away to Fulham in their last game before the international break.

stories.headline: NRL investigating after referee peppered with rubbish
stories.summary: Warriors great Shaun Johnson has labelled footage of fans throwing projectiles at referee Ashley Klein in Auckland as embarrassing, with the NRL investigating.
stories.body:
The NRL has been urged to come down hard on supporters who peppered referee Ashley Klein with projectiles as the league's integrity unit investigates the ugly aftermath of Newcastle's semifinal win over the Warriors.

Vision from Eden Park after fulltime in the Knights' 12-10 victory showed Klein being hit with a raft of bottles, cups and rubbish as he walked from the field.

The footage shows Klein having to be protected by security, as fans abused the veteran referee and projectiles rained down on him.

The NRL immediately launched an investigation into potential breaches of their spectators' code of conduct. An Integrity Unit investigator had been at the ground.

"If found guilty, they will be banned for a period of time from attending NRL games," ARL Commission chairman Peter V'landys told AAP.

V'landys' no-nonsense stance was welcomed by the referee's union, Professional Rugby League Match Officials (PRLMO), who called on the NRL to come down hard on the Warriors supporters.

"The safety of all referees and match officials is paramount, and they should be allowed to perform their duties without being placed in harm's way," PRLMO chair John Choueifate told AAP.

"To say I was disappointed is an understatement and call on the NRL to investigate the incident which detracted from an enthralling match.

"They need to send a very clear message to those responsible and to others in future that this rubbish must be stamped out of the game."

New Zealand Police confirmed no arrests were made, with "no issues to note" other than two pitch invaders.

The Warriors did not respond to AAP requests for comment.

Sunday's crowd of 48,511 marked the biggest ever for a rugby league match in New Zealand, after the NRL made the call to move the game from the Warriors' traditional Mt Smart Stadium home.

The NRL's investigation came as they admitted Klein had erred with a crucial decision not to penalise Newcastle prop Tyson Frizell for an escort in the dying minutes.

Had it been awarded, the Warriors could have levelled at 12-12 and sent the game to extra time. It's understood Klein will be dropped for the preliminary finals.

Regardless, Warriors great Shaun Johnson hit out at fans, labelling their behaviour as "embarrassing" and said a missed call was no excuse for that reaction.

"Ashley Klein is a human being in the middle of a park doing one of the toughest jobs there is," Johnson said on his Instagram.

"In what world do we think that is okay? You guys are so quick to point out that athletes and ex-athletes are role models for your kids.

"Well you're not setting the bar very high if that's what they've got to look up to. Be better man.

"It's such a s--- way to finish a season. Not just from a result standpoint. But leaving such a sour taste from a fan base. A fan base I deeply care about."

Warriors coach Andrew Webster had vented his frustration in the postmatch press conference, highlighting a bunker strip call on Te Maire Martin and the decision not to penalise Frizell for a possible escort on Leka Halasima.

The incident comes after AFL umpires also had cans thrown at them while leaving the MCG after Hawthorn's tight loss to Brisbane in Saturday night's preliminary final.

The AFL has also condemned the behaviour and warned of minimum five-year bans for any fans found responsible.

stories.headline: Sources: Saints LT Banks to have ankle surgery, out indefinitely
stories.summary: Saints left tackle Kelvin Banks Jr. is out indefinitely with a high ankle sprain and needs surgery, sources told NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.
stories.body:
New Orleans Saints left tackle Kelvin Banks Jr. is out indefinitely with a high ankle sprain and is expected to undergo surgery, sources told NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.

Banks' recovery would require time on injured reserve with a possibility to return late in the season, sources told Rapoport.

Banks suffered his injury late in the third quarter of the Saints' 24-17 win against the Baltimore Ravens. Banks landed awkwardly on his ankle and stayed on the ground after the play, eventually getting into a cart and leaving the field. Asim Richards took over at left tackle for the rest of the game.

Banks, 22, was the ninth pick of the 2025 draft and started all 17 games at left tackle for New Orleans last season. Taliese Fuaga, the Saints' 2024 first-round draft pick, started the 2024 season at left tackle but switched to right tackle last season.

stories.headline: Doc Rivers joins NBC as analyst, says coaching career over
stories.summary: Doc Rivers turned down an offer to become an NBA analyst for NBC after retiring as a player in 1996 because he couldn't promise then-NBC Sports chairman Dick Ebersol that he wouldn't become a coach.
stories.body:
Doc Rivers turned down an offer to become an NBA analyst for NBC after retiring as a player in 1996 because he couldn't promise then-NBC Sports chairman Dick Ebersol that he wouldn't become a coach.

With Rivers now insisting that his Hall of Fame coaching career is over, the time seemed right for him to join NBC.

The network announced on Monday that Rivers will be an analyst on games this season across NBC, Peacock and NBCSN, along with the possibility for some studio work.

"I honestly can say I'm absolutely retired," Rivers said in a phone interview with The Associated Press. "I had a long run. It ended up in the (Naismith) Hall of Fame (earlier this year) and I am so thankful that I was able to coach and played as long as I did. For the first time, I can focus on giving TV my 100% attention, which I'm really looking forward to.

"I think I've always been pretty honest. I've always celebrated the game in general, but told the truth. I don't think anyone has ever had a problem with honesty and the way you tell the truth. There are always times where you offend people because of the truth, but I've never really worried about that."

Rivers is sixth on the NBA's career coaching list in wins (1,194) and games (2,059). In nine seasons with Boston, he led the Celtics to the NBA title in 2008 and returned to the finals two years later. Along with Boston and Orlando, Rivers coached the Los Angeles Clippers, Philadelphia and Milwaukee.

This will not mark the first time Rivers has worked with NBC. He was a studio analyst during the 2012 London Games and got to do other sports beside basketball, including handball.

"We couldn't be happier to have him back on the NBC Sports team," NBC sports executive producer and president Sam Flood said in a statement about Rivers. "Having led the Celtics to the 2008 NBA title with nearly four decades of NBA experience between coaching and playing, we are excited to add another Hall of Famer to our roster."

Rivers was with Turner Sports for three years (1996-99) before beginning his coaching career with the Orlando Magic. He also had two stints with ESPN/ABC in 2003-04 and 2023. That included being on the top announcing team with Mike Breen and Doris Burke for the first couple months of the 2023-24 season before taking the Bucks job in January 2024.

"I don't take a lot of breaks in my life. I've always been around the game and this is a way of keeping me there," Rivers said. "When you think about it, I've played, I've coached, I've been in front office, I've done TV, I've done about everything you can do in our game. And that gives me an interesting perspective and hopefully I can share that with the viewers."

Rivers also coached five players who became NBC analysts and played against Reggie Miller, NBC's lead analyst. Rivers, a point guard, played on four teams during his 12-year career.

He coached his son, Austin, and Jamal Crawford with the Clippers; Grant Hill and Tracy McGrady in Orlando; and Brian Scalabrine with Boston.

One of the funnier moments last season was Austin Rivers trying to interview his dad before a Milwaukee-Cleveland game.

"With this opportunity, one of the things I thought was I'd love to work with Austin. That would be a lot of fun to be able to work with him," Doc Rivers said. "It's funny when you think about half the staff, I've either coached or been the father. I had a fight with Reggie, which is even funnier. So it's pretty cool how connected I am to all the talent."

NBC's coverage begins with three games on opening night, Oct. 20 - including Boston at Detroit and Oklahoma City vs. San Antonio. stories.headline: Toto Wolff warned Michael Masi against being 'stubborn, arrogant' before F1 2021 title controversy
stories.summary: Toto Wolff has claimed he repeatedly warned Michael Masi not to be "stubborn" or "arrogant" during the 2021 Formula 1 season.
stories.body:
Toto Wolff has claimed he repeatedly warned Michael Masi not to be "stubborn" or "arrogant" during the 2021 Formula 1 season, saying he tried to guide the former race director before the controversial title-deciding Abu Dhabi Grand Prix.

Masi broke the rules he was supposed to enforce around the safety car, forcing a final-lap restart at the end of the title decider between Lewis Hamilton and Max Verstappen.

Verstappen passed Hamilton on the lap to claim his first championship and to deny the then-Mercedes driver what would have been a record eighth title.

Wolff spoke about the controversy on the High Performance Podcast in 2024, where he was asked what the overriding emotions were at the time.

"Angry. Not anything [like] depressed or sad. Just angry," Wolff said. "Angry that an individual to take an eighth championship away from the best driver in the world by a decision."

Masi was removed from his role after the season and has not been back in a prominent motor racing position since.

Wolff went on to state that Masi, who joined SRO Motorsports Australia last week as head of sporting operations, is no longer relevant in the sport.

He explained that he had tried to help Masi and offered him counsel through the season and that the outcome was avoidable.

"I really tried to speak to Michael and guide him all along the year," Wolff said. "I said, 'listen I've been in the sport for a long time, listen to the drivers, don't always be stubborn in your decision making, don't be arrogant.'

"I tried that for the good of the sport, and obviously also for us as a team not to be vulnerable to situations that could be totally detrimental.

"So in that sense, this is just what happened is inexcusable. You could say empathy should make me realise how he feels. I realise how it feels. And I know that's not good, it's bad, but he could have thought about it all year long, when people, not only me, tried to support him in the right way.

Saunders: I raced against Verstappen ... for 10 seconds

- Hamilton clears the air on Ferrari replacements

- Norris: Monaco GP 2027 sprint 'exciting' for fans

"So sometimes you have to just realise that someone is just doing his own thing or taking his own decisions. So for me, I don't care about it anymore. Now you and I speak about it and we waste three minutes of our time, but he has no relevance."

Although Wolff said he is over it emotionally, there are regular reminders about what the team lost that day.

"Every week," he said when asked how often he thinks about it. "I mainly think about it because I think Lewis deserved to be the greatest of all time with eight world championship titles. And you can argue all along about that year.

"I think Max and Lewis were deserving champions. There were instances during the year where Max lost some points that he shouldn't have lost. You look at the crash in Monza both of them had. So both deserving champions, but on that particular afternoon in Abu Dhabi, it was unfair."
