stories.headline: Dreyer outduels Messi as San Diego hands Miami 4th straight draw
stories.summary: Lionel Messi scored his 101st goal for Inter Miami CF, but Anders Dreyer scored twice for San Diego FC, as the teams played to a 2-2 draw on Sunday night.
stories.body:
MIAMI -- Lionel Messi scored his 101st goal for Inter Miami CF, but Anders Dreyer scored twice for San Diego FC, as the teams played to a 2-2 draw on Sunday night.

It was Inter Miami's fourth consecutive draw in MLS play as new manager Kily González oversaw his first league game in charge of the club and cut a frustrated figure after conceding a late goal to drop points.

"We've been here for four days and haven't been able to train properly. Defensively, we really need to be much stronger," González said after the game. "We can't commit these defensive horrors, they come at a high cost. That final situation shouldn't have happened. It's surreal to be in a position to win the game, yet nearly lose it.

"We only avoided defeat because our goalkeeper saved us."

Dreyer gave San Diego a 1-0 lead in the 12th minute, capitalizing on a through ball from Jeppe Tverskov before deftly chipping over goalkeeper Dayne St. Clair.

Messi answered in the 24th with his 20th league goal of the season. His free kick from the right side went untouched through the penalty area and into the far side of the net, four days after he scored his 100th goal for Inter Miami in a 2-0 win over Mexican side Cruz Azul in the Campeones Cup.

"I think the Campeones Cup might have had an unconscious effect, especially in the first half, leading to a bit of complacency," González added. "These are factors that are part of football. At a club where we are obliged to win every match we play, we have to rise to the occasion. We made significant adjustments at halftime to get the team flowing and ensure we stayed compact, keeping the lines tight so we wouldn't suffer the way we did in the first half."

The goal was Messi's eighth from a free kick since entering the league in 2023, more than any other player in MLS during that time span.

Luis Suárez put Miami ahead in the 74th minute as Miami looked set to leapfrog New England into second place in the Eastern Conference, but Dreyer scored his second of the night eight minutes later with another fine finish -- this time from a ball over the top of the Herons' backline.

Miami is now in third place with a record of 12-4-10 with 46 points -- 11 behind first-place Nashville.

"But anyway, we have to keep going," González said. "On the positive side, we did some good things, but I need to fine-tune the defensive side because that's what really worries me most."

Earlier Sunday, FIFA announced that the final phase of the 2027 FIFA Women's Champions Cup will be played at Inter Miami's home of Nu Stadium in January. FIFA Chief Football Officer Jill Ellis spoke at halftime about bringing the competition to Miami.

"I think we've seen that this city loves its football. We've seen it this past summer with the World Cup," Ellis said. "I think it's time to bring a major women's tournament here to Miami. I think it's exciting."

Miami returns to MLS play next Sunday on the road against the Columbus Crew, while San Diego is also on the road with a game against Austin FC on Saturday.

ESPN writer Lizzy Becherano contributed to this report, while information from The Associated Press was also used.

stories.headline: UFC 331 takeaways: Are we living in the greatest era for lightweights?
stories.summary: Arman Tsarukyan and Joshua Van stole the show with emphatic statements at UFC 331.
stories.body:
The main card of UFC 331 had shocking moments on top of shocking moments on top of pound-for-pound resume building.

First, Sean Sharaf got his first UFC win as the biggest underdog in the promotion's history against Olympic gold medalist Gable Steveson in just 12 seconds. Then Arman Tsarukyan stepped into the cage for the first time this year and reminded everyone why the current crop of UFC lightweights may be the best ever. And flyweight champion Joshua Van followed it all up with a performance that should place him among the 10 best MMA fighters in the world right now. What more could an MMA fan want?

Van is a top five pound-for-pound fighter
I can't believe I'm saying this -- not because Van isn't great or hasn't been great for some time. It's just -- how does one become a top-five fighter in the world at age 24, with less than five years of pro experience?

After his performance on Saturday, I can't talk about Van anymore as just a phenom or a young champion. He is legitimately as good as just about anyone in the entire sport. Alexandre Pantoja coming off injury looked like the same Pantoja as before the injury. If anything, he looked even more determined than before. His pressure was appropriate and his decision-making was sound. Van was just better.

He defended takedowns and escaped on the ground when Pantoja could get him there. At one point, was it just me or did Van catch Pantoja's glove as he threw a punch, before countering? He caught some of Pantoja's kicks, in the same way he caught the one in December that led to Pantoja's injury. In the fifth round, when the result of the fight still felt up in the air, Van delivered his best five minutes of work, dropping Pantoja with a right hand.

Van is gifted athletically, confident and a natural finisher. He's been all of that from the first moment we saw him. One description that shouldn't be forgotten, however, is that he's extremely technical. This was one of the most technical fights of the entire year, against one of the best flyweights of all time, and Van ended up running away on the scorecards. If Van were 28, I don't think anyone would have an issue ranking him near the top of the pound-for-pound. The only hesitancy to do it is because -- it doesn't seem right or possible, given his age and relative inexperience. I'm getting over that. Van is top five. -- Brett Okamoto

Are we living in the greatest lightweight era of all time?

The history of the UFC's lightweight division is so undeniably rich. One of the division's greatest "eras" was from 2016 to 2020, when Conor McGregor became double champ at Madison Square Garden, Khabib Nurmagomedov dominated and timeless fighters such as Tony Ferguson, Dustin Poirier and Justin Gaethje were in their primes.

This upcoming chapter at lightweight has a chance to challenge all that.

Within the past three months, Ilia Topuria has suffered his first loss (in spectacular fashion to Gaethje on the White House lawn) and vowed revenge. Paddy Pimblett has turned in a star-making performance, submitting Benoît Saint Denis in less than a minute on a McGregor-headlined card. And now Arman Tsarukyan has completed an unbelievable walkoff knockout of Mauricio Ruffy. Topuria, Pimblett and Tsarukyan are three legitimate superstar storylines, and it just so happens they are all rivals who have promised to take each other out.

Don't forget that the champion, Gaethje, could postpone retirement in order to defend his throne. Veterans Max Holloway and Charles Oliveira are still active in the top five, too. Australia's Quillan Salkilld has had a breakout year, and Nurmagomedov's younger cousin, Usman, could potentially transition to the UFC after years of dominance in the PFL.

Yeah. The next few years could be the best in lightweight history, and that is really, really saying something. -- Okamoto

The Steveson train has hit an early crossroads

It's not like Steveson had never lost before. On his way to becoming a 2020 Olympic wrestling gold medalist and two-time NCAA Division I national champion, he was formidable but not perfect. His record at the University of Minnesota was 103-3. His international freestyle record, including cadet and junior levels, was 53-2. Even an all-time great has had to pick himself up and dust himself off at times.

But this defeat was different from whatever Steveson had ever experienced. He got knocked out cold in 12 seconds by Sharaf, a guy who came into their fight 0-2 in the UFC with both losses coming by knockout. Let's just acknowledge that this matchmaking was a setup to build an MMA résumé for Steveson. Considering that he had just four pro fights under his belt, though, this was an appropriate booking.

The result was a shocker. It was the largest known upset in UFC history, per DraftKings. But what's done is done, and the story now takes an unexpected twist. Will this be just a speed bump on Steveson's express road toward the top of the UFC heavyweight division? Or will this defeat make Steveson timid in standup fighting, slowing his development beyond being a one-dimensional wrestler? Heavy-handed UFC heavyweights will surely be emboldened by seeing Steveson crash to the canvas.

What seemed like a sure thing now is surrounded by question marks. The future might still be bright for Steveson. It probably will be. But here's a suggestion for Steveson: Don't bother watching the 12-second KO loss. Why put yourself through that again? Instead, go find video of Islam Makhachev's 2015 KO loss in his second UFC fight, then contemplate how Makhachev has managed to win all 17 of his fights since on his way to becoming the best pound-for-pound fighter in the sport. -- Jeff Wagenheim

stories.headline: Antoine Semenyo happy to lead Man City's attack if needed
stories.summary: Antoine Semenyo is ready to take on the challenge of leading Manchester City's attack if needed.
stories.body:
Antoine Semenyo is ready to take on the challenge of leading Manchester City's attack if needed.

The Ghana international underlined his finishing ability with two clinical strikes in City's thrilling 5-3 victory over Sunderland in the Premier League on Sunday.

The prolific output of Erling Haaland, who was also on target as Enzo Maresca's side maintained their 100% start to the campaign, means City are rarely short of goals.

But the club's summer transfer activity has left them with no clear replacement for Haaland should the Norwegian miss any games.

Maresca has identified winger Semenyo as the most obvious alternative and the 26-year-old would be happy to step up.

Semenyo said: "I've heard about his backup striker thing. I don't know where it's come from!

"But, yes, if I need to, then I'll do it. I've no problem in doing that."

Of his finishing, he added: "I think that just comes naturally.

"Once I'm in front of the goal, I know it doesn't move. So as long as I hit it in the corner, hit it with a good connection, I know it will go in."

City were pushed all the way by Sunderland, who showed no sign of weariness from their midweek Europa League outing.

Brian Brobbey scored a hat trick for the visitors but Semenyo's double and Haaland's late effort completed the job for City, for whom Enzo Fernández and Rayan Cherki also struck.

Both sides had numerous other chances in a frantic game. Haaland missed an open goal for City while Brobbey hit the bar and Rúben Dias had to clear off the line. Sunderland also felt they should have had a penalty for handball against Elliot Anderson.

Semenyo said: "It was a tough one. Physically, we knew it would be like that -- duels, aerial balls, set-pieces.

"We knew it would be a fight, and we just needed to stick together collectively and win our individual duels and get three points, which we've done.

"Sometimes it is going to be like that, not every game you can control. You just have to ride the waves. We knew if we got our chances, we would score."

- Erling Haaland sets unique goal milestone as Man City beat Sunderland

- Enzo Maresca relieved as Manchester City pass difficult Sunderland test

City have now won seven games in succession in all competitions since their defeat by Arsenal in the Community Shield.

With a three-point lead at the top of the Premier League, it has been a strong start under new manager Maresca but Semenyo feels there is still room for improvement yet.

He said: "Everyone feels good. It's where we want to be, but we're not going to get too complacent, too relaxed. We know that there's a lot more games to go.

"We just want to continue winning, we just have to keep going.

"It's seven or eight weeks we've been together now, so it's not been too long, but we're doing well. We're winning our games and we'll keep improving."

stories.headline: No decision made on banned five's future, say Swans
stories.summary: Zach Merrett has spoken glowingly of new Essendon coach Mark McVeigh amid rampant speculation that he will bid again for an AFL trade to Hawthorn.
stories.body:
Sydney's five exiled players have yet to be welcomed back to the AFL club amid speculation the Swans will reintegrate the suspended group.

Isaac Heeney, Chad Warner, Nick Blakey, Riley Bice and James Jordon have been absent from Swans headquarters since being suspended in August.

The five were stood down for breaching club standards following a postmatch party at the Pullman Hotel in East Melbourne.

Those suspensions are separate from a police investigation into sexual assault allegations, with Victoria Police flagging an update is not expected until late October.

No charges have been laid, and AAP is not suggesting any wrongdoing on the part of the five suspended players.

As the Swans head into exit meetings following last Friday's preliminary final loss to Fremantle, AFL.com.au reported on Monday the five were expected to return to the club this week.

But Swans chief executive Pavlich, speaking later on Monday before the Brownlow Medal count, said no decision on the five's reintegration had been made.

"We haven't confirmed that as yet. We're still working through the process," Pavlich told AAP.

"They're five of our players, five contracted players, people we've tried to support through this process.

"Their wellbeing, along with everyone impacted, has been at the forefront of our mind.

"So we'll continue to work through that."

All five are contracted for next year, with Blakey signed to the club until 2031.

Warner and Jordon come off contract at the end of 2027, while Heeney and Bice are signed until the end of 2028.

Blakey is reportedly seeking a trade to Victorian rivals, but football boss Leon Cameron has dismissed those rumblings as "speculation".

Victoria Police's eight-week timeline prediction on their probe of the Pullman Hotel incident -- which was first flagged on September 2 -- takes in the free agency and trade period from October 2 to October 14.

Main ball-winners Heeney and Warner weren't invited to the Brownlow function at Crown Palladium, but remained eligible for the award.

Heeney and Warner are expected to be frontrunners for Sydney's Bob Skilton Medal, to be held after this Saturday's grand final.

stories.headline: Borussia Dortmund teenager Konstantinos Karetsas returns to training after Champions League health scare
stories.summary: Borussia Dortmund says 18-year-old midfielder Konstantinos Karetsas is back in training just over a week after he slumped to the ground in an alarming medical incident on his Champions League debut.
stories.body:
Borussia Dortmund have said 18-year-old midfielder Konstantinos Karetsas is back in training just over a week after he slumped to the ground in an alarming medical incident on his Champions League debut.

Karetsas passed the ball to a teammate then signaled his distress to the referee before sitting on the grass during Dortmund's 3-2 win over Villarreal on Sept. 8.

He was in tears as he was stretchered off with suspected circulatory problems and was then taken to a hospital, where he stayed for much of last week.

"Konstantinos Karetsas is back in team training as of Wednesday after doing individual sessions at the start of the week," Dortmund said. "It was his first joint session with his teammates after he was taken off with circulatory problems in the game against Villarreal."

Dortmund hasn't specified the nature of any diagnosis for Karetsas, who was signed from Genk for a reported fee of $34.6 million last month, and didn't indicate whether he would be able to play Saturday against Stuttgart in the Bundesliga.

Karetsas plays internationally for Greece but was born in Belgium, where local media have reported that dehydration was suspected as a factor.

"I'm doing really well," he said in a video recorded during a visit to his old club Genk and published Monday on X. "We tested everything and everything is fine. I just need to adjust a bit to the intensity but that will come with time."

"I went out with him but in that moment, he wasn't able to speak," Book said.

- Borussia Dortmund teenager Karetsas hospitalised after slumping to turf in Champions League

Karetsas was able to cheer on his teammates from the stands in Saturday's 3-0 win over Paderborn.

Managing director Lars Ricken said there had been "no warning signs" of any circulatory problems prior to the incident.

stories.headline: Klein faces axe as NRL admit crucial refereeing error
stories.summary: The NRL is set to axe top referee Ashley Klein for the preliminary finals after admitting the Warriors were wrongly denied a crucial late penalty in their 12-10 semifinal loss to Newcastle.
stories.body:
The NRL is set to axe top referee Ashley Klein for the preliminary finals after admitting the Warriors were wrongly denied a crucial late penalty in their 12-10 semifinal loss to Newcastle.

NRL officials confirmed on Monday the Warriors should have been awarded a penalty with a minute left in Sunday's Eden Park thriller, for an escort infringement by the Knight's Tyson Frizell.

Had the penalty been awarded, the Warriors would have had the chance to level the scores at 12-12 via a penalty goal from just to the side of the posts and send the match to extra time.

But the call was instead missed on the field, with the bunker unable to review the play despite a stoppage for an injury soon afterwards.

A comprehensive NRL review of Newcastle's 12-10 semifinal did, however, back the bunker over two other contentious calls.

First, it was deemed that bunker official Chris Butler was right to rule Warriors centre Ali Leiataua got a thumb to a ball before it went to ground late in the match.

The NRL also supported the bunker's decision to stick with the on-field call of a strip against Warrior Te Maire Martin.

But it is the non-call on Frizell that will annoy the Warriors more.

The Newcastle veteran appeared to get in the way of Leka Halasima as he chased through on a kick in the Warriors' last attacking raid of the match.

Given the seconds that would have come off the clock while the Warriors lined up the shot, there would likely not have been time for a restart.

"I thought they were trying to find ways to take it off us," Warriors coach Andrew Webster said after the game.

"The last one, two points would have drawn the game, he is going across Leka, pretending to try and catch the ball which they've told us you can't do."

AAP understands Klein will pay for the error by losing his spot in the preliminary finals, with Grant Atkins or Gerard Sutton likely to be called up.

Klein has overseen every game of the past five State of Origin series and two of the last four Grand Finals.

He had been expected to referee last year's decider, before losing out to Atkins following 18 penalties in a Melbourne-Cronulla preliminary final.

Meanwhile, the NRL have threatened bans for fans who threw projectiles at Klein as he walked off Eden Park on Sunday night.

Vision showed a mass of bottles and rubbish being thrown at the long-time official, with Warriors great Shaun Johnson labelling the fans' behaviour "embarrassing".
